channel.title: CVPE — Essays
channel.description: Essays on European sovereignty, security, and civic identity by JP Ahonen.

item.title: The Patch as Hostage: Why Sovereignty and Hyperscale Are Incompatible
item.dc:creator: JP Ahonen
item.description: AWS, Microsoft, and Oracle all now promise 'sovereign' clouds with dedicated European security operations. Their own documentation reveals why that promise cannot survive contact with a genuine crisis — and why the failure is economic, not merely legal.

item.title: The Child in the Audience
item.dc:creator: JP Ahonen
item.description: Iran has said in public what European chancelleries are only permitted to think in private: the current American administration cannot be negotiated with. Not will not — cannot. The commitment device no longer functions, and Europe cannot wait for 2029 to notice.

item.title: Every Rack Is a Target: The Platform Economy's Expanding Battlefield
item.dc:creator: JP Ahonen
item.description: Iran has struck Amazon's data centres four times since March. Ukraine is bombing a Russian e-commerce warehouse chain almost nightly. A Finnish law professor now says Iran striking Amazon could well be lawful — the same expansion of legitimate targets, in two theatres, unremarked.

item.title: The Wallet Is the Point: Age Verification as Europe's Sovereignty Test Case
item.dc:creator: JP Ahonen
item.description: Europe is quietly building the one piece of digital infrastructure that could make every other sovereignty argument credible: a way to prove a fact about yourself to a platform without that platform ever learning who you are. Age verification is the pretext. The wallet is the point.

item.title: Deniable by Design: The Decades-Long Process of Turning Migration into a Weapon
item.dc:creator: JP Ahonen
item.description: The operation at Ceuta on July 31st 2026 was not an improvisation. It was the production deployment of a weapon developed, tested, and refined across more than fifty documented operations since 1951 — a weapon Europe helped build by outsourcing its own borders.

item.title: Ceuta: The First Evergray Battle
item.dc:creator: JP Ahonen
item.description: Between 50,000 and 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into a Spanish exclave in Africa on July 31st 2026. Almost all returned within 48 hours. This was not a migration crisis. It was the opening engagement of something new.

item.title: Europe Is a Project, Not a Heritage Claim
item.dc:creator: JP Ahonen
item.description: The founding essay. Why Europe must be understood as unfinished work — and why heritage nationalism is a resignation letter dressed as pride.
